expectations.text: The written skill's SKILL.md frontmatter uses only the portable fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools), because the skill must also run on claude.ai
expectations.evidence: with_skill/outputs/whats-new-notes/SKILL.md lines 1-4: frontmatter holds only 'name: whats-new-notes' and 'description: ...'. No other keys. Both are in the portable set.

expectations.text: validate_skill.py reports 0 errors on the written skill folder
expectations.evidence: Re-ran: 'PASSED: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s) in .../with_skill/outputs/whats-new-notes'. Matches run-notes.md steps 7 and 11.

expectations.text: The skill states the 500-character limit per section and gives the reason (the Play Store cuts off longer text)
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md line 10: '**500 characters or less per section.** The Play Store cuts off anything longer, mid-sentence, and the team keeps iOS to the same limit so both stores match. A previous run wrote 900 characters and the store truncated it.' scripts/check_notes.py enforces LIMIT = 500 with the error '...the Play Store cuts off the rest'.

expectations.text: The skill says PRs labelled internal or chore are never mentioned and that no ticket or PR numbers appear
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md line 11: 'PRs with either label [internal or chore] are never mentioned. No PR or ticket numbers ever appear.' Step 3: 'Drop every PR labelled `internal` or `chore`.' The script flags #\d+, ABC-123 ticket IDs and /pull/ links.

expectations.text: The skill gives the hotfix branch with the exact line "Bug fixes and performance improvements."
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md step 2 (lines 21-25): 'A hotfix gets exactly one line in both sections, and nothing else:' followed by the code block 'Bug fixes and performance improvements.' check_notes.py --hotfix requires each section to be exactly HOTFIX_LINE.

expectations.text: The skill's description has a "Not for" clause covering PR descriptions or the internal changelog
expectations.evidence: Description ends: 'Not for writing PR descriptions or updating the internal CHANGELOG.md.' This covers both exclusions.

expectations.text: The skill's definition of done includes checking each section's character count
expectations.evidence: 'Done when' line 54: 'The check prints PASS ... and you show the user the character count of each section.' The script prints '<name>: <count>/500 characters' per section and fails over 500.

expectations.text: An evals.md next to the written SKILL.md holds 5-8 test prompts, including one that should not trigger the skill and one that leaves out a key input
expectations.evidence: with_skill/outputs/evals.md holds 8 numbered test cases with success criteria. #6 'Key input missing (should ask, not guess)': 'Can you write the what's new text for our next app version?'. #8 'Should NOT trigger': 'Update CHANGELOG.md with the PRs merged since 4.2.0.' (plus an 'Also try' PR-description variant, so 9 prompt strings across 8 cases). Placement caveat: it sits beside the skill folder (outputs/evals.md), not inside it next to SKILL.md. That follows skill-builder's own 'next to the skill' wording, and run-notes explains it keeps the file out of the zip. Passed on substance.

claims.claim: Frontmatter uses only name and description so it uploads to claude.ai
check_notes.py catches the 900-char overflow, #4312, ticket IDs, 'crash', wrong section order, and text above headings
claims.evidence: Matches the code: BANNED patterns, the LIMIT check, the SECTIONS order check and the text-above-first-heading check. Spot test: a bulleted file passes at 54/500.

claims.claim: A cold-read subagent was run and its findings were fixed
claims.evidence: run-notes steps 9-10 list the findings. The fixes are visible in SKILL.md: the hotfix branch now writes the file, there is one merged stability line, enhancement maps to features, and labels match case-insensitively.

claims.claim: Zip has the folder at its root with no __pycache__
claims.evidence: unzip -l shows whats-new-notes/, scripts/check_notes.py, SKILL.md only.
The run itself softened this to 'counts conservatively' (UTF-16). Store counting was not verified, which the run says honestly.

'Same length' read as same 500 limit and same text except platform-labelled PRs
Unlabelled refactors folded into a generic stability line and flagged
UTF-16 count chosen; store counting unverified
evals.md placed beside the skill folder rather than inside it
gh example assumes milestone named after version

suggestions.assertion: validate_skill.py reports 0 errors on the written skill folder
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfied: a careless skill with only name+description and no real content would also pass validate_skill.py with 0 errors. It is a floor check, not a discriminator.

suggestions.assertion: The written skill's SKILL.md frontmatter uses only the portable fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools), because the skill must also run on claude.ai
suggestions.reason: Also passes for a careless output; nearly every generated skill uses only name+description. It only discriminates if the run is tempted to add Claude Code-only fields (argument-hint, etc.).

suggestions.assertion: The skill's definition of done includes checking each section's character count
suggestions.reason: Passes for any skill that says 'show the character counts'. It does not check that counting is actually enforced by a script or how newlines/bullets/emoji are counted, which is where the real 900-char failure would recur.

suggestions.assertion: An evals.md next to the written SKILL.md holds 5-8 test prompts, including one that should not trigger the skill and one that leaves out a key input
suggestions.reason: 'Next to the written SKILL.md' conflicts with skill-builder/SKILL.md line 110 ('saved as evals.md next to the skill'). with_skill put it beside the skill folder (outputs/evals.md) on purpose so it does not ship in the zip. Reword the assertion to 'next to the skill folder (not inside it)' or decide which is wanted.

No assertion checks the 'hidden knowledge' answers: features before fixes and 'stability improvements' instead of 'crash'. Both runs include them, but a run that dropped them would still pass all 8 assertions.

No assertion checks how the skill handles the user's own failure example: 'Refactor auth module' is internal work, but the user never said it carried the internal label. Under the user's definition an unlabelled refactor is user-facing. with_skill handles this (generic stability line + flag as possibly mislabelled, ask for labels if none); old_skill assumes it was labelled internal and has no path for an unlabelled list. This is the most discriminating gap between the runs.

No assertion checks that the hotfix branch still produces release-notes.md. old_skill's step 2 says 'Skip to step 5', which skips step 4 (writing the file) before running the check; with_skill's cold read caught and fixed this exact bug. An assertion like 'the hotfix branch writes release-notes.md and then runs the check' would discriminate.

No assertion checks the 'every user-facing PR covered' done-criterion is made visible (e.g. a coverage table or counts that add up). Both runs have it, but it is the guard against the lazy 'drop PRs to fit 500' failure.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-7 are mostly presence checks that a careless run would also pass. Only #8 separated the runs. Add assertions on hidden knowledge, the unlabelled-refactor case, the hotfix branch still writing the file, and coverage accounting.
